    Course Description & Information

    This course introduces the foundations and applications of computational intelligence, covering the history of AI, key concepts, and the role of intelligent agents. It explores uninformed and informed search algorithms, probabilistic reasoning, machine learning paradigms, neural networks, deep learning, enabling architectures, large language models, and computer visions. Through lectures and hands-on projects, students gain both theoretical and practical understanding of intelligent systems. The course culminates in an applied AI capstone project that integrates these methods to solve real-world problems. Prerequisite At least a C in CSCI 1302


    Course Learning Outcomes

    Upon completion of this course the students will be able to: 

    • Define the basic concepts and history of Artificial Intelligence and describe the role of intelligent agents.
    • Apply search algorithms to solve structured and unstructured problems.
    • Analyze and implement probabilistic models for decision-making under uncertainty.
    • Explain and utilized foundational machine learning models, including deep learning and reinforcement learning.
    • Develop and evaluate Natural Language Processing applications and understand the use of advanced models like Llama.
    • Apply deep learning techniques to both language and vision tasks.
    • Design, implement, and present a hands-on AI project that integrates multiple concepts from the course.

    Course-Level Expectations & Procedures

    EXPECTATIONS 

    Online courses are not self-paced and regular participation in online courses is required and will be recorded by your instructor. Students are expected to complete all course assessments using D2L. 

    Online learning assumes a high level of maturity and professionalism. It is designed to make learning more convenient but no less rigorous. The lack of a formal meeting schedule in an online course can be liberating. It can also be demanding because you must determine when to make time for class. Self-discipline and good time management skills are necessary when taking an online course. 

    Please remember that you will spend as much or more time completing an online course as you would taking it in a traditional face-to-face/classroom format. The special circumstances of taking an online course demand regular and consistent participation. Be sure to pace yourself throughout the semester making sure your responses to communications and assignments are timely. If you are not able to participate in any assigned class activities, you must contact your instructor immediately. 

    The instructor is required to report “no-shows” or students who do not show up the first day of class. Therefore, all students enrolled in the course must verify their enrollment. This can affect financial aid and you may be dropped from the class. Your instructor will notify you as to how to verify your enrollment before the beginning of the term to ensure that you are not reported as a “no-show”. 

    Course-Level AI Policy

    STUDENT USE OF AI IN COURSEWORK

    To maintain a culture of integrity and respect, generative AI tools should not be used in the completion of course assignments unless an instructor for a given course specifically authorizes their use. Some instructors may approve of using generative AI tools in the academic setting for specific goals. However, these tools should be used only with the explicit and clear permission of each individual instructor, and then only in the ways allowed by the instructor.

    Institutional Policies

    Accessibility Services

    Students with a documented disability must work with MGA's Accessibility Services to arrange essential services relating to their disability. All entitlements to accommodations are based on documentation and USG Board of Regents standards. If a student is considering requesting accommodations, contact Accessibility Services to discuss the process.

    If a student needs course adaptations or accommodations because of a documented disability or chronic illness, the student should notify their instructor in writing and provide a copy of a current Student Accommodations Report (SAR), which is available only from Accessibility Services. Faculty cannot offer accommodations to any student without timely receipt of the official SAR document.


    Artificial Intelligence 

    Follow the instructor's guidelines in the course syllabus for how students can or cannot use artificial intelligence tools and platforms to complete any coursework, activities, assignments, and assessments. MGA expects that all students use artificial intelligence ethically, responsibly, and in accordance with the guidelines for each course.


    Attendance Policy

    MGA students should attend all class sessions, be they face-to-face or online. Class attendance and participation is an individual student responsibility. Learn more about attendance expectations by asking each of your instructors and reading the Attendance Policy in the Academic Catalog.


    Nondiscrimination & Anti-Harassment Policy

    MGA is committed to ensuring a safe learning environment that supports the dignity of all members of the University community. We encourage students to read more about the Nondiscrimination and Anti-Harassment Policy.


    Student Code of Conduct

    MGA students are responsible for reading, understanding, and abiding by the MGA Student Code of Conduct.


    Plagiarism & Academic Integrity/Honesty

    MGA uses a plagiarism prevention service to evaluate written work that students submit for this course. The papers will be retained by the service for the sole purpose of checking for plagiarized content in future student submissions. MGA’s Code of Conduct prohibits the use of any unauthorized assistance in completing any work for any course. This assistance includes using artificial intelligence platforms to generate any part or all of student submissions. The Code of Conduct is available online.

    Student Support & Wellness Resources

    Academic Mindset

    The purpose of a university education is not just to teach you knowledge and skills but also to expand the ways you use your mind and handle challenges. A positive academic mindset provides an effective framework that will guide you through this course and also throughout your life as you adapt to a changing world. In this spirit, MGA seeks to encourage students to strengthen their positive academic mindset. This course promotes a positive academic mindset by highlighting the following:

    • Knowing that you can strengthen your abilities through effort and a positive attitude;

    • Believing in your own ability to learn and continue to improve;

    • Recognizing that the work in this course has value and purpose for you;

    • Fostering your willingness to embrace new experiences and challenges;

    • Acknowledging that your effort and attitude affect your performance.


    Academic Advising

    Academic advising at MGA supports students in setting goals, selecting majors, aligning career plans, and staying on track for graduation or certification. Each student is assigned an advisor based on their major and must meet with them at least once per semester.

    First-year students, students on probation, and those in learning support must meet every semester. Seniors should meet early in their final year and complete a degree audit—three semesters before graduation for bachelor’s students and two semesters for associate students. For details, visit the MGA Advising website.


    Withdrawing from a Course

    Before withdrawing from or dropping a course, students should check the last date for withdrawing before considering their options and the consequences of their choices.


    Course Experience Feedback Survey

    Student perception surveys of a class and its instructor are administered online at the end of each semester/session for all courses with five or more students. Students will receive an email containing a link to a survey for each course in which they are enrolled. All responses are anonymous.


    MGA Library 

    MGA’s five campus libraries provide access to print, electronic, and audiovisual resources, including databases, journals, and e-books via GALILEO and GIL-Find. Services include interlibrary loan, GIL Express, intercampus delivery, and research support from librarians (in person or online). Visit the MGA Library website or contact library@mga.edu or (478) 471-2709 for assistance.


    Mathematics Academic Resource Center (MARC)

    The MARC offers free tutoring for most math courses in person or online, by appointment or walk-in. We are equipped with computers, textbooks, whiteboards, calculators, and study notes to provide students with a space to study. For hours, locations, and booking a session, please visit the MARC website.


    Student Success Centers (SSC)

    The Student Success Centers provide students with free tutoring available online or face-to-face with professional and certified peer tutors as well as access to online study resources. To view contact information, subjects tutored, and tutor availability, visit the SSC website. 


    Writing Center 

    The MGA Writing Center is a free service that provides one-on-one consultations to assist students with all types of writing. Available in-person or via Teams, consultants provide feedback and use different strategies to help students improve their writing. Writing Center locations are open on the Macon and Cochran campuses. 


    School Closure & Weather Notifications (Knight Alert)

    MGA’s Knight Alert system provides free emergency notifications for severe weather, campus closures, and other safety alerts via call, text, and email. Students should update their contact information in SWORDS under Personal Information → MGA Alert Update Contact Information or by visiting the MGA Police Department webpage. 

    Students are also encouraged to download the free Rave Guardian app, select Middle Georgia State University, and enable features such as emergency alerts, safety timer, virtual escort, campus maps, and direct access to University Police or 911. For questions, contact MGA Police at (478) 934-3002.


    Student Life

    The Student Life Program is designed to offer students opportunities to interact with faculty, staff and other students outside the classroom setting, to provide students the opportunities to broaden their social and cultural experiences, and to help students become aware of and involved in community concerns. More information is available on the Student Life Program website.


    Well-Being and Mental Health Resources

    Counseling Services provides free confidential support for all enrolled MGA students through individual or group counseling, crisis intervention, and referrals. Students can discuss personal or academic challenges in a private setting and may request online appointments. Counseling Services is also proud to be a part of BeWell@MGA, which provides students 24/7 access to counselors and mental health resources to help cope with minor issues to major concerns. 


    Student Care

    If you’re facing personal, financial, or academic challenges that affect your success, Student Care can help. The office connects students with food assistance, emergency aid, housing and financial resources, success coaching, and other campus or community support. For assistance, email studentcare@mga.edu or call (478) 757-2264.
